cues: Catalysis is the change of rate caused by a catalyst.
A positive catalyst speeds a reaction up.
A negative catalyst, or inhibitor, slows it down, as glycerol does for hydrogen peroxide.
A promoter has no power of its own but boosts a catalyst, like molybdenum with iron.
And a poison destroys a catalyst, like arsenic oxide on vanadium pentoxide.
text: Catalysis is the change of rate caused by a catalyst. A positive catalyst speeds a reaction up. A negative catalyst, or inhibitor, slows it down, as glycerol does for hydrogen peroxide.
